newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia mulls rescue of Fokker - AWSJ.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia mulls rescue of Fokker - AWSJ.

text.p: Malaysia is studying a proposal on the possible rescue of bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker NV with a group of international partners, the Asian Wall Street Journal (AWSJ) reported on Wednesday.

Quoting senior officials in Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, the business daily said the Malaysian government's possible involvement would be through government investment firm Khazanah Holdings Bhd. Officials at the Prime Minister's department and Khazanah were not immediately available for comment.
"There is a proposal and it is being looked at seriously," a senior Malaysian administration official was quoted by AWSJ as saying.

Media interest in the plane maker was revived last week on news that Dutch industrial groups Stork and Begemann were in talks over Fokker. Stork bought Fokker's profitable maintenance and aircraft parts operations in 1996.

Dutch newspaper Algemeen Dagblad said on Thursday the discussions, which also involved a large Singaporean finance company, had reached a critical stage and had already lined up 400 million guilders. On Friday, Dutch Premier Wim kok said the government was pleased with the developments and would seriously consider any rescue package.
